related_questions.question: What is the new policy for Southwest Airlines?

text_blocks.snippet: Southwest Airlines is implementing several significant policy changes, including the introduction of assigned seating and changes to baggage fees and boarding procedures. These changes are part of a broader strategy to develop new revenue streams and improve the customer experience.
Here's a breakdown of the key changes:

list.snippet: Southwest will end its open seating policy and transition to assigned seating starting January 27, 2026.
Passengers will be able to choose from different fare bundles, including options with extra legroom seats.
The new boarding process will group passengers based on seat location, with priority given to those with extra legroom and loyalty program members.
Passengers can also pay for priority boarding.
The new boarding process will assign passengers a group number (1-8) instead of the current A-C system.
Southwest is ending its "bags fly free" policy.
Passengers will now pay to check bags, starting at $35 for the first bag and $45 for the second, according to USA TODAY.
Only passengers who purchase the highest fare tier (Choice Extra) will receive two free checked bags.
Southwest is also adjusting its boarding process, with priority given to those who choose seats with extra legroom and loyalty program members.
Passengers can book and reserve seats for after the January launch starting July 29, according to Travel + Leisure.
The airline is also making adjustments to cabin service, including earlier cabin preparation for landing.
